validated_results.title: Prediagnostic toenail cadmium and zinc and subsequent prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within the prospective CLUE II cohort assessing prediagnostic toenail zinc concentrations and subsequent incident prostate cancer risk, providing a target-specific trend result.

extraction.comparison_type: Increasing toenail zinc concentration quintiles (top four fifths vs bottom fifth; trend across fifths)
extraction.design: Nested case-control study within a prospective cohort
extraction.timing: Toenail samples collected at baseline in 1989, prediagnostic
extraction.population: Men in the prospective CLUE II study

sample_size.excerpt: Included in the analysis were 115 prostate cancer cases and 227 age-matched controls nested in the prospective CLUE II study located in Washington County, MD. Participants provided toenail samples at baseline in 1989.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 115 + 227 = 342

cases.excerpt: Included in the analysis were 115 prostate cancer cases and 227 age-matched controls nested in the prospective CLUE II study located in Washington County, MD.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated from conditional logistic regression models.

p_value.excerpt: did not decrease with increasing concentrations of zinc (P trend = 0.2)

comparison.excerpt: For both metals, the ORs for the top four fifths were each below 1.0 when compared with the bottom fifth.

design.excerpt: 115 prostate cancer cases and 227 age-matched controls nested in the prospective CLUE II study

validated_results.reason: Pooled prospective cohort study of alcohol amount and beverage type with incident prostate cancer, reporting beverage-specific risk estimates.

extraction.population: 12,989 subjects drawn from three different cohorts

sample_size.excerpt: The study population consisted of 12,989 subjects drawn from three different cohorts. During a mean follow-up of 12.3 yr, 233 subjects developed prostate cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Furthermore, drinkers of more than 13 beers, 13 glasses of wine, and 13 drinks of spirits had a risk of 1.03 (CI: 0.67, 1.60), 0.92 (CI: 0.42, 1.99), and 1.01 (CI: 0.52, 1.98), respectively, compared with abstainers of the given beverage of alcohol.
